chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلِيَّ بْنَ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ اسْمِ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ قَالَ: سَالِمُ بْنُ مُكْرَمٍ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: ثِقَةٌ؟ فَقَالَ: صَالِحٌ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ، وَكَانَ جَمَالًا، وَذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ حَمَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ. قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: لَا تَكُنِّ بِأَبِي خَدِيجَةَ. قُلْتُ: فَبِمَ أَكْتَنِي؟ فَقَالَ: بِأَبِي سَلَمَةَ. وَكَانَ سَالِمٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ، وَكَانَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ يَوْمَ بَعَثَ عِيسَى بْنُ مُوسَى بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْعَبَّاسِ، وَكَانَ عَامِلَ الْمَنْصُورِ عَلَى الْكُوفَةِ إِلَى أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ، لَمَا بَلَغَهُ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ أَظْهَرُوا الْإِبَاحَاتِ وَدَعَوَا النَّاسَ إِلَى نُبُوَّةِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ، وَإِنَّهُمْ يَجْتَمِعُونَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَلَزِمُوا الْأَسَاطِينَ يُورُونَ النَّاسَ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ لَزِمُوهَا لِلْعِبَادَةِ، وَبَعَثَ إِلَيْهِمْ رَجُلًا فَقَتَلَهُمْ جَمِيعًا، لَمْ يَفْلِتْ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ أَصَابَتْهُ جِرَاحَاتٌ فَسَقَطَ بَيْنَ الْقَتْلَى يُعَدُّ فِيهِمْ، فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ فَتَخَلَّصَ، وَهُوَ أَبُو سَلَمَةَ سَالِمُ بْنُ مُكْرَمَ الْجَمَالُ الْمُلَقَّبُ بِأَبِي خَدِيجَةَ. فَذَكَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ تَابَ وَكَانَ مِنْ مَنْ يَرْوِي الْحَدِيثَ

translations.en: I asked Aba al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan about the name of Abi Khadija; he said: Salim ibn Mukram. I said to him: Is he trustworthy (Thiqa)? He said: He is good (Salih). He was from the people of Kufa and was a cameleer. It was mentioned that he carried Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Mecca to Medina. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim informed us from Abi Khadija that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: Do not use Abi Khadija as a kunya (agnomen). I said: With what should I be known? He said: With Abi Salama. Salim was among the companions of Abu al-Khattab, and he was in the Masjid on the day Isa ibn Musa ibn Ali ibn Abdallah ibn al-Abbas was sent to Abu al-Khattab (as governor of al-Mansur over Kufa), when it reached him that they had manifested the permissibility of forbidden acts and called the people to the prophethood of Abu al-Khattab, and that they were gathering in the Masjid and clinging to the pillars, making people think they were clinging to them for worship. So he sent a man to them who killed them all. No one escaped except one man who was injured, fell among the dead and was counted among them. When night covered him, he emerged from among them and escaped. That man was Abu Salama Salim ibn Mukram the Cameleer, who was nicknamed Abi Khadija. It was mentioned after that that he repented and became among those who narrate the Hadith.

en.summary: This Rijal narration from Kashshi highlights Salim ibn Mukram’s transition from a prominent follower of Abu al-Khattab’s millenarian movement to a trusted Hadith narrator, illustrating the political volatility of the Kufan scholarly milieu. The Imam’s directive to change his kunya from 'Abi Khadija' to 'Abi Salama' likely served to distinguish him from the earlier, more controversial figure or to mark his spiritual reorientation after the massacre. His survival among the dead and subsequent repentance underscore the theme of divine preservation for those who remain faithful amidst sectarian upheaval.
en.seo_question: Who was Abi Khadija and what was his relationship with Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.صالح: Good/Competent (a slightly lower grade of reliability than Thiqa)
key_terms.كنية: Agnomen (a name starting with Abu or Umm, used as a nickname)
key_terms.أبو الخطاب: Abu al-Khattab (a leader of the Khattabiyya sect in Kufa)
key_terms.إباحات: Permissibility of forbidden acts (a key doctrine of the Khattabiyya)
